known_losses: Fine source bevels, ridges and curved CAD tessellation are reduced per semantic region.
Open vendor CAD seams are inherited; only closed components have a positive-volume claim.
Normals are recalculated coherently with 70-degree hard-edge policy, not exact original corner-normal byte preservation.
Voxel-repaired skins can round or close details near/below 1.5mm (Go2 front covers 0.7mm); keeping bounds is not proof of full surfaces, apertures or physics clearance.
Two individual Go2 thin sensor covers use source-vertex convex skins; their small recesses simplify without joining regions or links.
Go2 low tier omits the decorative white torso wordmark; medium/high keep sampled source material regions.
The lowest tier uses coarse local silhouettes and material subdivisions; small logos, fastener shapes and ports can deform.

recipe_rationale: Different budgets for torso, motor hip covers, long thigh, lower leg/foot and each arm segment.
Allocate every connected CAD region by surface area and extent, with a minimum region floor; no minimum-area component deletion.
Repair defective large CAD skins locally at 1.5mm voxel size before bounded semantic collapse; Go2 front slotted covers use 0.7mm. Thin sensor plates are excluded.
Closed source/repaired skins receive explicit triangles and direct local collapse; planar dissolve is excluded because it broke thin closed skin topology.

Go2 grey front joint covers get extra semantic budget and source-surface vertex projection; retained hip/thigh vertices stay within source coordinate bounds. This is not box reconstruction or proof of all surface/clearance preservation.
The low-tier 1500 URI is a nominal target only; joint connections and clean major shells take priority over the revoked hard cap.
